extracted.intended_audience: news editors, newsroom leaders, and working journalists
extracted.subtask_description: A set of principles and professional standards for journalists and news organizations governing responsibility, independence, accuracy, impartiality, and fair conduct in news gathering and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: PREAMBLE
rubrics_metrics.description: The First Amendment, protecting freedom of expression from abridgment by any law, guarantees to the people through their press a constitutional right, and thereby places on news people a particular responsibility. To this end the American Society of News Editors sets forth this Statement of Principles as a standard encouraging the highest ethical and professional performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalism requires industry, knowledge, and a pursuit of integrity proportionate to the press's public obligation; the Statement is presented as an aspirational baseline for ethical and professional performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARTICLE I - Responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary purpose of gathering and distributing news and opinion is to serve the general welfare by informing the people and enabling them to make judgments on the issues of the time. Newsmen and women who abuse the power of their professional role for selfish motives or unworthy purposes are faithless to that public trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News organizations should prioritize public service over private or commercial interests; the press should bring independent scrutiny to power, including official conduct at all levels of government.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARTICLE II - Freedom of the Press
rubrics_metrics.description: Freedom of the press belongs to the people. It must be defended against encroachment or assault from any quarter, public or private.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists must be alert to ensure public business is conducted in public and vigilant against any parties who would exploit or encroach on the press; defending press freedom is a professional obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARTICLE III - Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must avoid impropriety and the appearance of impropriety as well as any conflict of interest or the appearance of conflict. They should neither accept anything nor pursue any activity that might compromise or seem to compromise their integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain both actual independence and the appearance of independence: avoid gifts, activities, or relationships that could create conflicts of interest or the perception of compromised integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARTICLE IV - Truth and Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Good faith with the reader is the foundation of good journalism. Every effort must be made to assure that the news content is accurate, free from bias and in context, and that all sides are presented fairly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the same factual standards to editorials, analysis, and commentary as to news reports; correct significant errors of fact and errors of omission promptly and prominently.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARTICLE V - Impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: To be impartial does not require the press to be unquestioning or to refrain from editorial expression. Sound practice, however, demands a clear distinction for the reader between news reports and opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure clear labeling and separation of opinion/personal interpretation from straight news reporting; impartiality requires transparency about when content is interpretive or editorial.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARTICLE VI - Fair Play
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should respect the rights of people involved in the news, observe the common standards of decency and stand accountable to the public for the fairness and accuracy of their news reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give persons publicly accused the earliest opportunity to respond; honor pledges of confidentiality to sources and do not grant them lightly; identify sources of information unless there is a clear and pressing need for confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose/Intent of the Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: These principles are intended to preserve, protect and strengthen the bond of trust and respect between American journalists and the American people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The principles exist to sustain public trust essential to the freedom of the press; they are normative guidance for behavior and decision-making in newsrooms.
